items.title: Integrate Trusted Types in webpack
items.body:
*Edited*: Updated the description to match the newest rebase logic.

Note: This is a rebase of the PR #9426  for webpack 5. Recent changes introduce the compatibility with importScripts and the Worker loading code.

## Trusted Types
[Trusted Types](https://web.dev/trusted-types) is a Web API aimed to make applications resilient against DOM XSS by guarding how DOM XSS sinks are used, and in specific - how scripts are loaded in a web application. 

Applications that enforce [Trusted Types](https://web.dev/trusted-types) by using ['require-trusted-types-for'](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Content-Security-Policy/require-trusted-types-for) CSP directive cannot currently use webpack's chunk/module loading mechanism. Two things violate Trusted Types:

 - `LoadScriptRuntimeModule.js` assigns a string to a `script.src` sink (this is used e.g. by `JsonpChunkLoadingPlugin`),
 - In `WorkerDependency.js` worker constructors are called with a string,
 - `ImportScriptsChunkLoadingPlugin.js` calls `importScripts` with a string. 

These violations block applications enforcing Trusted Types from using webpack. 

**What kind of change does this PR introduce?**

This PR causes Webpack to use a Trusted Types API, when available in the runtime environment (e.g. in current Chrome, Edge, Opera, Brave, or via polyfill) to instantiate a [Trusted Types policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-trusted-types/dist/spec/#trusted-type-policy)  and pass all script URLs through it before reaching the aforementioned sinks. Each realm (for example, worker realm for workers that would use `importScripts`) gets its own policy instance under the same name. 

The policy name can be configured via output options `trustedTypesPolicyName` setting. By default it's `webpack`. 

This makes applications using webpack compatible with CSP `require-trusted-types-for 'script'` or even more restrictive `require-trusted-types-for 'script'; trusted-types webpack`. This setting guarantees to applications that only the scripts bundled by webpack can be dynamically loaded, greatly reducing the security review surface for applications.

**Did you add tests for your changes?**

Yes. We've also verified this e2e against Angular builds using webpack 5.

**Does this PR introduce a breaking change?**

**No**. Trusted Types support is feature-tested. For environments without Trusted Types support the code uses strings as usual - the code is as such backwards-compatible. The only change is a slight increase in the runtime loader size, if the loader uses one of the sinks. If needed, we could look into optimizing this as well.


**What needs to be documented once your changes are merged?**

The new configuration option: `output.trustedTypes` to enable trusted types

* `output.trustedTypes: true`: Uses `output.uniqueName` as policy name
* `output.trustedTypes: string`: Uses the passed string as policy name
* `output.trustedTypes: { policyName?: string }`: The normalized advanced format

items.title: feat(DefinePlugin): Support array as value in DefinePlugin
items.body:
**What kind of change does this PR introduce?**

Currently, _DefinePlugin_ doesn't support array as value. Let's see this example:

```js
new DefinePlugin({ ITEMS: [1, 2, 3] })
```

We get:

```js
{ '0': 1, '1': 2, '2': 3 }
```

With these changes, we get:

```js
[1, 2, 3]
```

**Did you add tests for your changes?**

Yes

**Does this PR introduce a breaking change?**

Potentially, yes. Because before, an array was handled as an object

**What needs to be documented once your changes are merged?**

We can add information about using array in _DefinePlugin_, [here](https://webpack.js.org/plugins/define-plugin/#usage)

items.title: Asset modules enhancement
items.body:
<!-- Thanks for submitting a pull request! Please provide enough information so that others can review your pull request. -->
<!-- Explain the **motivation** for making this change. What existing problem does the pull request solve? -->
<!-- Try to link to an open issue for more information. -->


<!-- In addition to that please answer these questions: -->

**What kind of change does this PR introduce?**

Feature

It works but there is some stuff to do:
- [x] fix tests
- [x] add more tests
- [x] add generator option validation by a scheme

**Did you add tests for your changes?**

Yes

**Does this PR introduce a breaking change?**

No

**What needs to be documented once your changes are merged?**

`experiments.asset: true` activates 3 new module types

* `type: "asset/resource"` emits a separate file and exports the URL (like url-loader)
* `type: "asset/inline"` exports a DataUrl of the asset (like url-loader)
* `type: "asset"` automatically chooses between DataUrl and separate file (like url-loader with limit)
* `type: "asset/source"` exports the source code of the asset (like raw-loader)

for `asset` there is this parser option (`Rule.parser`):

* `dataUrlCondition`: `{ maxSize: number } | (source: string | Buffer, { filename: string, module: NormalModule }) => boolean`
  * `maxSize`: maximum size in bytes of an asset where a DataUrl is used
  * function: a function deciding

for `asset/inline` and `asset` there is this generator option (`Rule.generator`):

* `dataUrl`: `{ encoding: "base64" | false, mimetype: string } | (source: string | Buffer, { filename: string, module: NormalModule }) => string`
  * `encoding: "base64"`: DataUrl is base64 encoding (default)
  * `encoding: false`: DataUrl is url encoding
  * `mimetype`: custom mimetype, otherwise by extension
  * function: a function generating the DataUrl

items.title: feat: getOptions util for loader
items.body:
<!-- Thanks for submitting a pull request! Please provide enough information so that others can review your pull request. -->
<!-- Explain the **motivation** for making this change. What existing problem does the pull request solve? -->
<!-- Try to link to an open issue for more information. -->

New `getOptions` util for loader (part of migration loader-utils into core)

<!-- In addition to that please answer these questions: -->

**What kind of change does this PR introduce?**

feature

**Did you add tests for your changes?**

Yes, after feedback i will add more tests

**Does this PR introduce a breaking change?**

No

**What needs to be documented once your changes are merged?**

`getOptions` now in core as part of loader context and have this function signature -> `this.getOptions(schema?: JSONSchema)`.

It differs from the `getOptions` from schema-utils. Upgrading a loader to the new `getOptions` is a breaking change for these reasons:

* It's only supported in webpack 5.
* Instead of JSON5 it only support JSON as query string `?{arg:true}` -> `?{"arg":true}`
  * Hopefully nobody writes inline loader query strings this way anyway.
  * Using JSON should considered as deprecated and not be promoted in the loader documentation
* loader-utils has some special behavior for parsing query strings (`true` `false` and `null` won't be parsed as string but as primitive value). This is no longer the case for `this.getOptions` which uses native querystring parsing (from node.js).
  * Special handing can be added in loader code after getting the options
* Schema is optional, but when doing a breaking change anyway, please add schema validation for your options.
  * The `title` field in the schema can be used to customize the validation error message: e. g. `"title": "My Loader ooooptions"` will display errors like `Invalid ooooptions object. My Loader has been initialised using an ooooptions object that does not match the API schema. - ooooptions.foo.bar.baz should be a string.`

items.body:
Fixes the `ResolveOptions.plugins` types to use a plugin that takes in a resolver plugin instead of a compiler plugin.
